name: Ensemble — many cards authored, one bundle compiled
thesis: The owner is right that the product should be a fleet of specialists with their own tools that hand off to each other, authored in the studio; the prior review is right that swapping cards mid-call breaks the voice prompt cache (voice/bot.py builds one system_instruction per call at line 525 and flows_dynamic sets role_message only on the entry node), fragments the audit trail (interactions.deployment_id, call_attempts.deployment_id and voice_sessions.deployment_id all hold exactly one id today) and multiplies eval suites (card.eval.suite_id per card, G7/G8/G-OB9 per publish). Ensemble resolves this by separating the authoring unit from the runtime unit. Authors keep composing Agent Cards (agent_core/cards/schema.py AgentCard stays the unit of identity, tools.include, skills, handoffs, human_gates, outbound.objectives) and wire them on an Ensemble canvas; the publish compiler (agent_core/cards/compile.py G0-G15/G-OB1-9, wrapped by a new agent_core/ensemble/compile.py with gates G-E1..G-E11) flattens the reachable closure from one Door card into one Bundle: one stable system prefix, one namespaced FlowGraph (flow_graph.py; each specialist's prompt_versions.flow becomes a subgraph, each CardHandoff becomes an edge with a compiled carry action), one per-node tool offer table, one grant-by-specialist table, one prompt_versions.compiled row, one bot_deployments id. The runtime never swaps agents, processes, prefixes or voices: a hop is a developer-block replacement plus a grant pointer change, which is exactly the mechanism voice already uses for skills (voice/tools.py:2812-2833 load_skill -> replace_developer(SKILL_BODY_PREFIX)). The mental model the owner wants ("specialised agents with specialised tools, no hardcoded flow, studio-driven") is literally what the author sees and edits; the thing the bank runs is one mouth executing one compiled graph. What is gained: prefix-cache survival across hops, one deployment id per call, one canary per ensemble, one red-team surface with incremental slices, deletion of the Redis-dependent mesh. What is lost and priced honestly: a specialist cannot be deployed independently of the ensembles that include it, and there is no true parallel consultation between specialists on a live call.
primitives: Specialist Card — owns identity, tools.include/locked, skills[], connectors[], human_gates[], memory, eval (contract suite), and its own subgraph (prompt_versions.flow) and brief (prompt_versions.prompt, now a token-capped developer delta rather than a system prompt). File: agent_core/cards/schema.py AgentCard, unchanged shape plus `identity.kind: Literal['door','specialist','closer','internal']`. Today's intake-v1 / kaia-v2-4 / insurance-v1 / supervisor-brief (agent_core/cards/defaults.py:36-45) become the first four rows, seeded to the DB instead of held as Python constants.

Handoff Edge — owns the transition between two specialists: condition (model prompt, expression over flow_graph SESSION_VARIABLES such as call_goal_intent/intent/identity_verified, or always), typed payload, carry mode, target entry node, optional return. File: schema.py CardHandoff gains `mode: Literal['model','expression','always']`, `clauses[]`, `carry: Literal['brief','summary','full']`, `entry_node: str`, `return_to: str|None`, `voice_change: bool=False`; `payload_schema` (already present) compiles into the transition tool's properties. Compiles to a `go_to_<slug>.<node>` FlowsFunctionSchema exactly like flows_dynamic.py:_transition_tool, plus pre_actions.

Door — the entry subgraph that owns greet/disclose/discover_intent/verify_identity and a `route` node whose outgoing edges are the ensemble's first hops; also owns the shared terminal nodes (pre_close, call_ended, terminate_politely, escalate_close — all in flow_graph.RESERVED_NODE_KEYS). File: today's Intake card (defaults.py:158-174, purpose 'Identify the caller, disclose recording, route to a specialist') plus the door portion of voice/flows.py materialised via voice/flow_export.py. One door per ensemble (G-E2).

Ensemble — owns the composition: door bot_id, member closure, entry bindings (channel/number -> door; objective -> mission owner), voice, and the publish lifecycle. New file agent_core/ensemble/schema.py `Ensemble(door_bot_id, members[bot_id], voice_bot_id, bindings[])`; stored as the door card's published prompt_versions row plus a new `entry_bindings` table (id, tenant_id, channel, address, objective, entry_bot_id, environment). Replaces agent_core/cards/routing.py runtime_entry_bot_id() and .env.example:108 BOT_ID.

Bundle — the compiled artifact the runtime loads: {schema_version, prefix_text, prefix_hash, graph (FlowGraph v2: node keys namespaced `<slug>.<key>`, edge.data.handoff{to_slug, carry, voice_change, payload}), specialists{slug: {bot_id, prompt_version_id, card_hash, flow_hash, brief_message, persona_delta, skills[]}}, grant_union[], grant_by_specialist{slug: [...]}, offer_by_node{node_key: [...]}, missions{objective: node_key}, post_call{on_outcome[]}, human_gates{tool: require}, report: CompileReport}. Lives in a new column `prompt_versions.compiled jsonb` on the door's published version; `bot_deployments.bundle_hash text` pins it; agent_core/deployment.py load_active_bundle returns it as bundle['compiled'].

Static Grant vs Active Grant — Static Grant (publish-time union, what G4/G6/G9 gate) and Active Grant (the grant of the specialist currently speaking, what may_execute enforces). File: agent_core/tools/grant.py ToolGrant gains `for_specialist(bundle, slug, channel)`; voice/tools.py ToolState gains `active_specialist: str` and the `keep = allowed | ALWAYS_ON` filter at tools.py:2918 becomes a per-turn lookup into grant_by_specialist. This is the prerequisite ADR-0001 names ('a mid-call handoff changes the card and must change the grant') fulfilled without a process swap.

Mission Entry — owns which subgraph a dialled call starts in. File: mission.py build() reads the ensemble's mission-owner card via entry_bindings(objective); card.outbound.objectives[].entry_node resolves against the compiled graph's `missions` map (G-E9 re-runs G-OB2 on the flattened graph); call_attempts.bot_id = door bot, call_attempts.deployment_id = ensemble DEP (columns exist, sql/21_outbound.sql:30-31).

Carry — what crosses a hop: `brief` (deterministic developer block rendered from VoiceSession facts + flow variables + payload, zero inference), `summary` (LLMSummarizeContextFrame via the existing summarize_context action, bot.py:1498-1512, run under the bridge line), `full` (nothing folded). File: voice/flows_dynamic.py compiles carry into pre_actions on the target's entry node; bot_runtime.py walker renders the same block on the text path.

Closer — post-call: call_closer.py (one call_outcomes row per attempt) + post_call_actions.py (authored verbs) read bundle.post_call, which the compiler merges from door + specialists (G-E7). Unchanged modules; new input.

Text Walker — the pipecat-free interpreter of the same compiled graph for WhatsApp: new backend/flow_walker.py, state (node_key, variables, active_specialist) persisted in bot_turn_state (bot_runtime._bot_state), reusing voice/flow_vars.evaluate_condition semantics. Replaces the intent->skill map INTENT_TO_SKILL in agent_core/skills/runtime.py:27-35 with authored expression edges.

Trace — per-turn attribution: bot_tool_calls.agent_id (exists, sql/12_crosscutting.sql:148) = active specialist slug, skill_id = active skill; interaction_handoffs (sql/04_interactions.sql:61-77) gains turn_index, deployment_id, carry and reason values 'specialist_route','specialist_return','mission_entry'. interactions.handler_bot_id stays the door (the accountable mouth).
runtime_model: INBOUND VOICE. (1) Twilio media socket arrives; voice/bot.py resolves the bundle with load_active_bundle(bot_id=agent_core.ensemble.routing.resolve_entry(channel='voice', address=to_number)) instead of load_active_bundle('production') at bot.py:427 (which today falls to db.DEFAULT_BOT_ID = kaia-v2-4 and is why Intake receives nothing); canary hash-split by customer_id stays in agent_core/canary.pick_deployment_id; the result is one DEP id, stamped on voice_sessions.deployment_id and interactions.deployment_id as today. (2) System prefix = bundle.compiled.prefix_text: door prompt + guardrails (agent_core/prompt.build_voice_system_prompt) + door persona + the sorted skill description_block of the door and shared skills (skills/runtime.py description_block). The prefix is byte-identical for every call on this DEP, so the cache is warm across calls, not just across turns. The mission briefing that bot.py:566-571 appends to the system prompt today moves to a developer block (replace_developer('MISSION', ...)) so per-borrower text never touches the prefix. (3) build_authored_flow(session, compiled.graph, objective='inbound') — unchanged engine (flows_dynamic.py), bigger graph; entry = door isStart node. (4) Door: greet_disclose -> discover_intent (capture_call_goal writes session.call_goal_intent, already in flows_dynamic.SESSION_VARIABLES) -> verify_identity -> route. The route node's outgoing edges are compiled from the door's handoffs[]: expression edges on call_goal_intent (payment_intent -> collections.state_position, product_faq -> insurance.entry, hardship -> hardship.intake) fire deterministically via the existing _advance_action post-action; model-chosen go_to_<slug> transition tools cover the ambiguous case. (5) Specialist: its subgraph runs; each node offers node.data.tools ∩ Active Grant plus its transitions (flows_dynamic.py:415-435); skills load as today via load_skill; locked engines are on every specialist's grant by G3. (6) Hop: an edge fires -> pre_actions [tts_say bridge line (node.entryLine), carry action, specialist_enter(slug)] -> replace_developer('ACTIVE SPECIALIST', brief+persona_delta), ToolState.active_specialist = slug, RTVI emits flow.specialist, CrmSink queues an interaction_handoffs row (from_bot_id=door, to_bot_id=specialist, reason='specialist_route', turn_index, deployment_id) off the audio path. (7) Close: every specialist exit edges to a door-owned terminal (G-E2); end_call goes through the close probe and _node('call_ended') as today (tools.py:2853-2879); CrmSink complete -> call_closer.py (queue = call_attempts.closed_at IS NULL; inbound calls must reserve an attempt row with purpose='in_session' in Phase 0 so both directions are closed the same way) -> post_call_actions run bundle.post_call rules -> call_outcomes.actions_applied. OUTBOUND MISSION. (1) treatment/enact.py enact_one -> outbound.place: reserve call_attempts row, contact_policy.admit at send time (unchanged), mission.build(card=mission owner resolved by entry_bindings(objective), deployment_id=ensemble DEP) writes call_attempts.context.mission; attempt_id/objective/treatment_decision_id ride the Twilio stream params (bot.py:482-500). (2) Voice worker loads the same bundle by call_attempts.deployment_id (pinned at dial, so a publish mid-campaign cannot change a live attempt's version), reads the mission, sets session.extra['entry_node'] = compiled.missions[objective] (e.g. 'bounce.open' inside the Bounce specialist's subgraph; the outbound door confirm_identity nodes are shared via entryFor as today) and build_authored_flow(objective=..., entry_node=...). (3) Mission latches survive hops: upsell_blocked='mission_forbids_offers' (bot.py:557-561), max_duration_sec budget, expected_customer_name — all on VoiceSession, never on a card. (4) Hops identical to inbound (bounce_cure -> hardship declared -> hardship.intake with carry='brief'). (5) Close identical; cadence.py reads call_outcomes and retries the same mission only. WHATSAPP TURN. bot_runtime.handle_turn today does prompt+tools with no flow (bot_runtime.py:909-949). Under Ensemble it loads the same bundle (load_active_bundle(bot_id=resolve_entry('whatsapp', to_number))), then flow_walker.step(state, compiled.graph, understanding): render the current node's developer task message and the ACTIVE SPECIALIST block into _build_messages, offer node tools ∩ Active Grant ∩ CATALOG.for_channel(TEXT) plus go_to_* transitions as OpenAI tools, run the existing chat_with_tools loop, evaluate expression edges after each tool result (flow_vars.evaluate_condition) and on turn end, persist {node_key, variables, active_specialist} in bot_turn_state, write bot_tool_calls.agent_id. 'say' nodes send the literal text; entryLine/respondImmediately are voice-only and ignored (G-E11 warns when a node used on the whatsapp channel depends on them). Handoff on text is the same edge, same interaction_handoffs row, same grant swap.
studio_model: FLEET INDEX (Habibi/src/routes/agent-studio.index.tsx) groups cards by Ensemble rather than by reachability lozenge: 'Inbound servicing (door: Intake)', 'Outbound collections (owner: Collections)', 'Internal (Supervisor brief, Clerk)'. The routing states in agent_core/cards/routing.py collapse to entry / member / unbound; 'direct' disappears because a specialist never holds a production deployment of its own. CARD EDITOR keeps the 15 tabs in prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:1109-1132 but re-scopes four of them by identity.kind: System Prompt becomes 'Brief' on a specialist (a developer delta, linted to a token cap, with the lint message 'this is not the system prompt; the door owns it'); Voice shows 'inherits ensemble voice' unless an inbound edge sets voice_change; Outbound is enabled only on the card that owns missions; Bindings and Ship move to the ensemble. AGENT GRAPH TAB becomes the real thing — EnsembleCanvas.tsx replacing the body of AgentGraphTab: nodes are member cards drawn as collapsed subgraphs (fed by a new GET /agent-studio/ensembles/{door_bot_id}/graph that returns the compiled closure instead of main.py:2272-2298's 'all cards + this card's handoffs'), edges are Handoff Edges with an inspector for condition (prompt text / expression clauses over SESSION_VARIABLES / always), carry, payload fields, entry node, return_to, voice_change; double-click a member opens its Flow tab (existing FlowCanvas/FlowInspector in components/flow); a 'Compile' button calls POST /agent-studio/ensembles/{door}/compile and paints per-edge and per-member gate status; a 'Flattened view' toggle renders the compiled FlowGraph read-only in FlowCanvas so the author sees exactly what the borrower will traverse. SHIP TAB (ShipTab.tsx) is ensemble-scoped: one traffic_pct, one auto_rollback list, one experiment row per door bot. TO ADD A SPECIALIST an insurance ops lead: (1) Fleet index -> New card -> template 'Lapse Specialist' (agent_core/cards/templates.py:41-46, clone_card creates a bots row + draft version); (2) Flow tab: author entry node and an exit node; (3) Skills tab: attach insurance-lapse, doc-fulfil (signed packs); Tools tab: include stays inside catalog; (4) Brief tab: write the persona delta; (5) 'Mark publishable' runs the member static gates G0/G1/G3/G4/G5/G9/G10 plus the specialist's contract suite (code graders, seconds); (6) open the Ensemble canvas of 'Inbound servicing', drag an edge from collections.negotiate_ptp exit to lapse.entry, set condition expression `intent equals upsell_opportunity` and a model fallback prompt, carry=brief, payload {reason}; (7) Compile — the report lists G0-G15, G-OB1-9 on the synthesized union card and G-E1..11; (8) Ship at 10% with auto_rollback [live_qa_burn, third_party_leak]; publish writes one prompt_versions.compiled and one bot_deployments row. No code was written; no waiver, product or contact time became authorable. COMPILER CHECKS (agent_core/ensemble/compile.py, run after cards/compile.py per member and once on the synthesized union card): G-E1 closure — every member reachable from the door by edges, no orphan; G-E2 one door, terminals owned by the door, every specialist exit edges to a terminal or a return; G-E3 identity-before-writes on the compiled graph — every path from the door start to any node offering a non-read tool passes verify_identity (or the member is flagged pre_identity_safe and offers only read/KB tools), which keeps disclosure-before-identity mechanical; G-E4 reserved-key ownership — each flow_graph.RESERVED_NODE_KEYS key defined by at most one member, because voice/tools.py transitions by name; G-E5 prefix budget — door+shared skill descriptions ≤ CATALOG_PREFIX_TOKEN_CAP (800, skills/lint.py:10) and every node's offer ≤ tools.max_voice_tools (per node, not per card); G-E6 voice coherence — members whose voice differs from the ensemble voice warn unless the inbound edge sets voice_change; G-E7 post_call merge — no two rules for one outcome with contradictory verbs; G-E8 human_gates — for the same tool the strictest require wins ('both' > 'floor'/'identity'); G-E9 mission ownership — each Objective claimed by exactly one member and G-OB2 re-run on the flattened graph; G-E10 member pins — each member's prompt_version is published and its contract suite report is pass; G-E11 text-walkability — nodes reachable on the whatsapp channel do not depend on voice-only tools or entryLine.
handoff_mechanics: WHAT CHANGES ON A HOP. Prompt: the system message does not change — it is bundle.prefix_text for the whole call; the developer block tagged 'ACTIVE SPECIALIST' is replaced (not appended) via the existing replace_developer path (bot.py:835-851 replace_developer_block; the same mechanism the CRM card and SKILL_BODY_PREFIX use), carrying the specialist's brief (its former system prompt, capped by lint at ~400 tokens) and persona delta; the node's task_messages come from the compiled subgraph as on any transition. Tools: the Pipecat node's functions list is the target node's compiled offer (node.data.tools ∩ grant_by_specialist[slug] plus transitions), and ToolState.active_specialist = slug makes may_execute consult grant_by_specialist — so the receiving specialist brings its own grant, as CONTEXT.md defines Handoff, without a second process. Flow: the transition is an ordinary flow_manager.set_node_from_config into a node of another subgraph; deterministic edges fire via _advance_action, model edges via go_to_<slug>.<node> whose properties are the CardHandoff.payload_schema (typed carry, stored into flow variables). Voice: unchanged by default (one TTS stream); an edge with voice_change=True compiles a TTSUpdateSettingsFrame pre_action after the bridge line, and G-E6 requires the bridge line so the borrower hears the introduction before the new voice. Context: carry='brief' renders a deterministic developer block from VoiceSession (identity_verified, outstanding, call_goal, understanding.intent/sentiment/language), the flow variable bag and the edge payload — zero inference; carry='summary' queues LLMSummarizeContextFrame (bot.py:1498-1512) and the compiler requires an entryLine on the target so the ~600-900 ms summarization runs under speech; carry='full' folds nothing. WHAT IT COSTS (C1). Prefix cache: the system message bytes are identical before and after the hop, and identical across calls on the same DEP, so the cached prefix survives every hop; the suffix changes every turn anyway. Per-hop added tokens: ≤ ~400 (brief) + the target node's task message; a second hop replaces rather than adds. Extra inference on the audio path: none for brief/full; one summarization for summary, overlapped with the bridge line. Registry swap: a dict pointer. Audit write: queued through CrmSink, off path. No worker handover, no Redis, no LLMWorker activation (voice/workers/insurance.py, mesh_bus.activate_and_publish and the mesh_activate_insurance action at bot.py:1518 are deleted). What the hop does not preserve: nothing beyond what a normal node transition already discards; the KV cache of the conversation suffix is rebuilt every turn today. Prefix ceiling: the union of skill descriptions in the prefix is capped at 800 tokens (G-E5); specialist-scoped skills therefore ride in the ACTIVE SPECIALIST block rather than the prefix, which means the model learns of them at the hop rather than before it — acceptable because the hop is the trigger, and stated as a limit. ON THE TEXT PATH the same edge produces the same developer block and grant swap inside flow_walker.step; there is no cache to protect and no voice to change.
audit_model: One version number per call by construction. bot_deployments has exactly one active row per (door bot, environment) (uq_bot_deployments_bot_env_active, sql/09_bot_config.sql:257-259); its prompt_version_id points at the door's published prompt_versions row whose new `compiled` column pins every member as {bot_id, prompt_version_id, card_hash, flow_hash} and carries prefix_hash and the full CompileReport (G0-G15, G-OB1-9, G-E1-11) — the compiler artifact stops being thrown away, extending what agent_core/change_log.py already does for gate outcomes. bot_deployments.bundle_hash = sha256(compiled) and change_log COMPONENTS gains 'compiled', so the tamper-evident hash chain (audit_log entity, seq-ordered) covers the flattened graph, not just the door's prompt. Every runtime row already stamps the DEP: interactions.deployment_id (sql/04_interactions.sql:25), voice_sessions.deployment_id, call_attempts.deployment_id (pinned at dial, so a mid-campaign publish cannot retroactively change a live attempt), and eval_reports.prompt_version_id. A regulator asking 'why did this borrower get this sentence / this offer / this call at this time' is answered in one join: the sentence -> interaction_transcript turn -> interaction_handoffs (turn_index ≤ turn) gives the active specialist and the carry mode, bot_tool_calls.agent_id/skill_id gives which specialist and which skill invoked which tool; the offer -> offer_decisions (reco) referenced from the recommend_next_offer tool call, which the grader product_in_reco already pins; the call at this time -> call_attempts.decision_id -> treatment_decisions.id + policy_version, plus contact_policy's contact_events row; and all of them carry the same DEP id, which resolves to one compiled bundle and, through it, to the exact member versions and the gate report that let it ship. interactions.handler_bot_id stays the door (the accountable mouth) rather than flipping per hop as db_inbox.handoff_to_agent does today (db_inbox.py:1479-1492), so analytics keyed on handler_bot_id (db_bot_analytics.py:332) do not fragment; specialist attribution lives in interaction_handoffs and bot_tool_calls, which are per-event rather than per-interaction. Canary keeps the invariant: deployment_experiments is keyed by the door bot and pick_deployment_id returns one DEP per customer hash. The eval side stops guessing: eval/run.py bot_id_for_suite's name-match hack (run.py:14-34) is replaced by eval_reports.bot_id = door bot and a new eval_reports.scope jsonb naming the member slugs the run covered.
policy_model: Nothing an author or a hop can do widens what the engines decide. Locked engines: G3 runs per member card (LOCKED_POLICY_ENGINES on tools.locked, all six PolicyBindings 'required'), and the compiler additionally asserts every grant_by_specialist entry contains the locked mouth tools (LOCKED_MOUTH_TOOLS) — recommend_next_offer and evaluate_authority remain the only speakers of product and rupee amount on every subgraph; the treatment engine still decides whether a call happens (treatment/enact.py enact_one, contact_policy.admit at send time) and no edge, carry or post_call verb can schedule a dial except through cadence -> contact_policy (post_call_actions.py rule 1). Grant: the Active Grant is compiled statically from the target card ∪ its signed packs ∪ its connectors ∪ VOICE_ALWAYS (grant.py:for_card), so a handoff moves to a pre-gated set and can never union onto the source's — the property ADR-0001 requires. Offer ⊆ grant is preserved per node. Identity-before-writes becomes a compiled-graph property, not a prompt convention: G-E3 walks every path from the door's start to any node whose offer contains a non-read tool and requires a verify_identity node on it (the built-in verify tool sets session.identity_verified, which every write tool already checks), and a specialist entered before verification must be flagged pre_identity_safe and may offer only read/KB tools; human_gates are merged strictest-wins (G-E8) and enforced at execution by the same handlers as today. Mission latches are session state, not card state: allowed_offers=[] -> upsell_blocked (bot.py:557-561), NEVER_OFFER (mission.py) and pool_kind='service_1600' zeroing offers all survive any number of hops because VoiceSession is the one object every subgraph closes over. Contact time: never authorable in an edge or a subgraph — cadence.py may only retry the same mission and contact_policy re-admits at dial time; the compiler refuses a post_call verb outside POST_CALL_ACTIONS ∪ the union grant (G-OB6 on the union card). Model-chosen edges are typed tools with payload_schema properties, so prose cannot hand off (grader no_prose_handoff stays in the contract suite), and the free-target handoff_to_agent(target_bot_id) tool is retired because a model picking an arbitrary bot id is exactly what compiled edges make impossible.
eval_model: Three tiers, only the top one costs LLM time, and only the changed slice runs by default. Tier 1 — member static gates on every save: G0 schema, G1 flow validity, G3 bindings, G4 tools ⊆ catalog, G5 handoff targets exist, G9 signed skills, G10 connectors, flow_graph.validate_graph; milliseconds, already implemented in cards/compile.py, exposed on the specialist's card as 'Mark publishable'. Tier 2 — specialist contract suite: code graders only (agent_core/eval/graders.py verify_before_ptp, no_prose_handoff, product_in_reco, crm_card_injection, plus new grant_respected — every tool call in the fixture ∈ grant_by_specialist[slug] — and handoff_via_edge_only — no interaction_handoffs row without a go_to_* call), run by run_suite_fixtures over the specialist's fixtures with the specialist's compiled offer_by_node; seconds, no model; eval_suites.kind='capability' rows scoped to the slug; required green for G-E10. Tier 3 — ensemble regression + redteam + outbound (G7/G8/G-OB9 on the synthesized union card, same flags eval_gate_enabled / redteam_gate_enabled / outbound_eval_gate_enabled): eval_tasks and eval_redteam_cases gain `scope jsonb` ({specialists:[slug], edges:[edge_id], door:true}); the ensemble compiler diffs member card_hash/flow_hash against the previously published compiled bundle and the scheduler runs only tasks whose scope intersects changed members, plus every task scoped to the door and every redteam case scoped to a changed or new edge; the report records scope so a partial run is never mistaken for a full one. The full ensemble suite runs nightly unchanged (eval/schedule.py run_continuous, redteam never skippable) and is required for a promote from canary to 100%. Canary: one deployment_experiments row per door bot covers every specialist; adding a specialist adds no experiment; rollback triggers keep their vocabulary (ROLLBACK_TRIGGERS) and live_qa_burn is attributed per specialist through bot_tool_calls.agent_id and interaction_handoffs so the Ship tab can say which member burned. Marginal cost of a specialist = Tier 2 (seconds) + the Tier 3 slice tagged to it and to its edges; sub-linear in specialists because the door, the terminals, the locked engines and the shared skills are tested once per ensemble rather than once per card. Honest floor: red-teaming a new handoff edge is genuinely new work (an injection at the boundary is a new attack surface), and the nightly full run still scales with total fixtures; the design makes the default publish cheap, not the total verification free.
migration: Phase 0 — seams, no behaviour change (flag ENSEMBLE_ENABLED off). Add agent_core/ensemble/{schema,compile,routing}.py producing a compiled bundle for a single-card ensemble (door = the card itself), sql migration adding prompt_versions.compiled jsonb, bot_deployments.bundle_hash, entry_bindings, eval_tasks.scope, interaction_handoffs.turn_index/deployment_id/carry and the reason CHECK values; agent_core/deployment.py load_active_bundle returns bundle['compiled']; voice/bot.py and bot_runtime.py read compiled.graph when present, else flow (today's path). Move the mission briefing from the system prompt (bot.py:566-571) to a developer block; reserve a call_attempts row for inbound calls so call_closer.py covers both directions. Ships alone; reversible by ignoring the new column.

Phase 1 — real in-process handoff on voice. voice/flows_dynamic.py compiles edge.data.handoff into pre_actions (bridge line, carry, specialist_enter); voice/tools.py ToolState.active_specialist and grant lookup replace the one-shot keep filter at tools.py:2918; agent_core/tools/grant.py for_specialist; interaction_handoffs written via CrmSink; bot_tool_calls.agent_id populated. Delete voice/mesh.py, voice/mesh_bus.py, voice/mesh_roles.json, voice/workers/insurance.py and the voice_insurance compose service, agent_core/cards/defaults.py BOT_TO_MESH_ROLE, agent_core/cards/handoff_policy.py, the mesh_activate_insurance action (bot.py:1514-1540). The four first-party cards are published as a one-member-each ensemble so behaviour equals today; reversible by ENSEMBLE_ENABLED=false (single-card compile) — the mesh deletion itself is git-reversible only, and the mesh is dead code today (active_role is read by nothing that changes tools or prompt).

Phase 2 — the Door and ensemble routing. Materialise the door portion of voice/flows.py into Intake's flow via voice/flow_export.py, add the route node, publish the first real ensemble 'Inbound servicing' = Intake -> {Collections, Insurance}; entry_bindings rows per (channel, number); agent_core/ensemble/routing.resolve_entry replaces runtime_entry_bot_id() (cards/routing.py:34-44) with BOT_ID as fallback until the table is populated; new routes /agent-studio/ensembles/{door}/graph|compile|publish in main.py; EnsembleCanvas.tsx replaces the AgentGraphTab body; ShipTab scoped to the door. risks: Loss of independent specialist deploy: a fix to one specialist requires republishing every ensemble that includes it (one DEP each), and a specialist shared by three ensembles is three publishes; incremental evals and the ensemble canary make each cheap, but the owner should hear that 'publish the Lapse specialist' is not a single action.

No true parallel consultation: specialists are sequential in one context. 'Agents communicate among themselves' is realised as typed edges with carried payload and shared session state, not message passing between live agents; internal agents (supervisor brief, clerk) stay out-of-band on work_runtime. If the owner's mental model requires two specialists reasoning concurrently on a live call, this design says no on purpose.

Prefix budget is a hard ceiling: 800 tokens of skill descriptions (G-E5) means specialist-scoped skills ride in the ACTIVE SPECIALIST block, so the model cannot proactively load them before the hop; a large ensemble also grows the union prefix, which caches but still bills tokens per turn.

Reserved-key coupling: voice/tools.py transitions by name (_node('negotiate_ptp')), so only one member may define each RESERVED_NODE_KEY (G-E4); a second collections-like specialist must use unreserved keys and the built-in begin_* tools will not route to it until Phase 5 retires the name-based transitions — a real refactor of voice/tools.py.

Developer-block accumulation under summarisation: brief/persona deltas replaced via replace_developer must fold safely when LLMSummarizeContextFrame collapses history (the VS-0D653BF9C3 class of stale-fact assertion); carry='summary' must be authored with a bridge line or it adds 600-900 ms on the audio path.

flow_walker.py is a third interpreter of the flow semantics (data shared, engine new): respond_immediately, pre_actions and entryLine have no text analogue and divergence from Pipecat behaviour is likely without the conformance suite; WhatsApp is the weakest link in this design.

Audit drill-down depends on ordering: CrmSink writes asynchronously, so specialist attribution must join on turn_index, not wall clock; forgetting this yields a sentence attributed to the wrong specialist.

Constants-to-rows migration touches every card_for() caller and the boot re-seed; a half-migrated state where the DB row and the Python constant disagree is exactly the drift the compiler exists to prevent — the seed must be idempotent and hashed.

Cache assumptions: Azure prompt caching is best-effort and needs ≥1024 identical prefix tokens; vLLM prefix caching on open weights hits on identical token prefix per replica — both hold for this design, but per-replica warmth means the first call on a cold replica pays full price; there is no cross-replica warm pool here.

Incremental evals can hide cross-specialist regressions (a door edit changes which specialist is reached); mitigated by always running door- and edge-scoped tasks and the nightly full suite, but a publish between nightlies is verified on a slice.

Operator concepts: expression edges over SESSION_VARIABLES, carry modes and reserved-key ownership are new vocabulary for a collections head; the canvas must hide them behind defaults (carry=brief, condition=intent picker) or authorability degrades.
score_self: C1 Voice latency: 5 — a hop is a developer-block replacement plus a grant pointer, zero added inference by default; the system prefix is byte-identical across hops and across calls on one DEP once the mission briefing leaves the system prompt; the only inference-bearing carry mode is overlapped with a required bridge line.

C2 One version number per call: 5 — one bot_deployments id per (door, environment) by the existing unique index, pinned on interactions/voice_sessions/call_attempts; prompt_versions.compiled pins member versions and the gate report; specialist attribution is per-event (interaction_handoffs, bot_tool_calls.agent_id) so the trail never forks.

C3 Policy engines stay the deciders: 5 — G3 per member plus locked tools asserted on every compiled grant; grants are static per specialist and a hop can only move to a pre-gated set; G-E3 makes identity-before-writes a graph property; mission latches live on the session; free-target handoff_to_agent is deleted.

C4 On-prem deployability: 5 — Postgres columns and one Pipecat process; the Redis mesh, LLMWorker sidecar and bus are deleted rather than made optional; open-weights prefix caching benefits from the same identical-prefix property.

C5 Operator authorability: 4 — templates, the Ensemble canvas, per-edge inspector and named gates keep the studio the only path and let an ops lead add a specialist without code, but expression edges and carry modes are new concepts and G-E4 will surface reserved-key errors that need plain-language guidance.

C6 Eval cost sub-linear: 4 — contract suites are LLM-free and per-specialist, ensemble regression/redteam run only the changed slice by default, and one canary covers the fleet; the honest residue is that new edges need genuinely new red-team cases and the nightly full run still grows with fixtures.

C7 Migration realism: 4 — six phases, each behind a flag or a fallback, starting from files that exist (compile.py, flows_dynamic.py, deployment.py, defaults.py, mesh.*), with Phase 1 removing code that is provably inert today; Phase 5's retirement of name-based transitions and flows.py is the heavy, less reversible tail.

C8 Inbound and outbound and WhatsApp: 4 — door, mission entry via entry_bindings and compiled missions map, carry on every hop, and the Closer reading merged post_call are concrete; WhatsApp gains a real flow engine for the first time but as new code whose parity with Pipecat semantics must be earned by a conformance suite.
